basic_information.short_title: Removal of the “None of the Above” Ballot Option
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT REMOVING THE “NONE OF THE ABOVE” OPTION FROM THE OFFICIAL BALLOT IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 14, ARTICLE VII OF BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 35, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “BANGSAMORO ELECTORAL CODE OF 2023”
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately upon publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or on its official website

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Takes the “None of the Above” option off the ballot for Bangsamoro parliamentary elections. Voters can no longer formally register a vote rejecting all the candidates.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act itself gives no reason. It states the change and directs COMELEC to revise the ballots immediately; the enacted text carries no declaration of policy or explanatory section.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Official ballots carry the names of candidates, and party logos for political party representatives — and nothing else. Any ballot design including a “None of the Above” choice must be revised.
who_will_be_affected: Every voter in Bangsamoro parliamentary elections
COMELEC and the Bangsamoro Electoral Office, which must revise the ballots
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Immediately on publication — the act does not wait the usual 15 days.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. You can no longer vote for “None of the Above” in a Bangsamoro parliamentary election. The ballot lists candidates and party logos only.
in_practice: Official ballots contain the names of the candidates
For political party representatives, the ballot includes their party logos
No ballot may include a “None of the Above” option
COMELEC, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office, must revise the ballots immediately
The act took effect immediately on publication, not after the usual 15 days

for_specific_groups.Voters: Your options are the candidates listed. There is no longer a formal way on the ballot to record that you reject all of them.
for_specific_groups.Voters who would have chosen it: An abstention or a spoiled ballot is not the same thing — neither is counted as a deliberate rejection of the field.
for_specific_groups.Candidates and parties: No candidate can now be outpolled by 'None of the Above'.
for_specific_groups.COMELEC: Immediate revision of the official ballots is required.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Bangsamoro parliamentary elections in the BARMM.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: At the ballot box, from the first parliamentary election held after publication.
what_you_can_do: Expect a ballot listing candidates and party logos only
Ask the Bangsamoro Electoral Office about the revised ballot design
watch_out_for: The act states no reason for the change — there is no policy declaration in the enacted text.
It took effect immediately rather than after the usual 15 days.
It removes a voter option shortly before the region's first parliamentary elections under the Electoral Code.
The act says nothing about how abstentions or blank votes are to be treated in place of the removed option.

key_terms_explained.None of the Above: A ballot choice letting a voter formally reject every candidate listed, as distinct from not voting or spoiling a ballot.
key_terms_explained.Bangsamoro Electoral Code of 2023: BAA 35, the region's own election law, which this act amends.
key_terms_explained.Bangsamoro Electoral Office: The COMELEC office for the region, responsible here for revising the ballots.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Sha'ban 09, 1447 / 28 January 2026, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 11 February 2026.

benefits.headline: A simplified ballot carrying candidate names and party logos.

direct_benefits.benefit: Party logos on the ballot for political party representatives

indirect_benefits: A single, uniform ballot design across the region's parliamentary elections
limitations: It removes a voter option rather than adding one.
No reason for the removal is stated in the act.
No replacement mechanism for registering rejection of all candidates is provided.

for_citizens: None. The act changes what is on the ballot, not what a voter must do.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no offence for voters. Its prohibition falls on the ballot itself: no official ballot may include the “None of the Above” option.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Bangsamoro Electoral Office of the Commission on Elections
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A voter who dislikes every candidate in their district previously had a “None of the Above” box. Under this act that box is gone; the remaining choices are the listed candidates, an abstention, or a spoiled ballot — and none of those is recorded as a rejection of the field.
A voter looking for a party rather than a name will find party logos beside political party representatives on the revised ballot.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 14, Article VII of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 35, the Bangsamoro Electoral Code of 2023, by transferring Section 14 of Chapter 1 to Chapter 2 of Article VII and renumbering it as Section 1 of that Chapter, to read: the official ballots for BARMM parliamentary elections shall contain the names of the candidates, and for political party representatives shall include the logos of their respective political parties.

Section 2 — The Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office, shall cause the immediate revision of the official ballots for BARMM parliamentary elections to ensure that no ballot includes the “None of the Above” option.
Section 4 — Repeals or modifies inconsistent laws, decrees, executive orders, rules and regulations.
Section 5 — Takes effect immediately upon publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or on its official website.

impact.figures_note: The act appropriates no funds. Ballot revision costs are not addressed.

related_legislation.related_note: Amends the Bangsamoro Electoral Code of 2023 (BAA 35), which established the region's own election law ahead of its first parliamentary elections.

implementation_status.irr_status: None required by the act; COMELEC is directed to revise the ballots immediately.
implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. This is among the first acts signed by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua and Speaker Mohammad S. Yacob, and marks a change of both offices from the acts of earlier sessions.

citizen_questions.q: Can I still vote “None of the Above”?
citizen_questions.a: No. The act removes that option and directs COMELEC to revise the ballots so that no ballot includes it.

citizen_questions.q: What is on the ballot now?
citizen_questions.a: The names of the candidates, and for political party representatives the logos of their parties. Nothing else.
The act does not say. Unlike most Bangsamoro acts it carries no declaration of policy or explanatory section — it states the change and directs the ballot revision.

citizen_questions.q: Is spoiling my ballot the same thing?
citizen_questions.a: No. A spoiled or blank ballot is not recorded as a deliberate rejection of all candidates, which is what the removed option allowed. The act provides no replacement for that.
Immediately upon publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or on its official website, rather than after the usual 15 days.
